Enduring Value, 
Expanding Horizons
Mobility is no longer a backdrop to economic 
growth — it is its engine. Across infrastructure 
corridors and digital supply chains, through the 
shift to cleaner energy and the rising demand 
for smarter, safer movement of goods, 
mobility is rewriting the rules of commerce 
and connectivity.
India stands at the centre of this 
transformation. What was once seen as just a 
cost-efficient manufacturing base has become 
one of the world’s most influential arenas for 
mobility innovation — a nation building not 
just roads and networks, but the future of how 
economies move.
Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles has grown 
alongside this ambition and shaped it. For 
decades, we have been more than a vehicle 
manufacturer. We have been a trusted 
partner to the businesses, transporters and 
entrepreneurs who keep this nation’s supply 
chains alive. That trust is not incidental to our 
business. It is the foundation of it.
Enduring Value, Expanding Horizons reflects 
where we stand today: a Company with 
the heritage to anchor confidence and the 
capability to pioneer change. Our enduring 
value lies in what our customers have always 
counted on — high reliability and uptime, 
low total cost of ownership and an expansive 
network that stands behind every vehicle we 
sell. Our expanding horizons are defined by 
where we are taking them next — advanced 
powertrains, connected and intelligent 
vehicles, greener platforms and solutions 
engineered for the demands of tomorrow.
We are expanding  our portfolio and 
deepening our presence, at home and in 
global markets, not by chasing scale alone, but 
by creating solutions that genuinely add value 
to our customers’ businesses. Every design 
decision, every powertrain choice, every 
service innovation is anchored in one question: 
does this make our customers conduct their 
business better?
Guided by our promise of Better 
Always, we enter this next chapter 
with clarity of purpose:  to deliver 
mobility solutions that create lasting 
value, open new possibilities and 
power the progress of a nation on 
the move.

About the Report
Tata Motors Limited’s 2nd Integrated Annual Report for FY26 covers our financial and  
non-financial performance and provides an insight into our business model, strategy, risks, 
opportunities, performance and achievements during the period under review.

During the year, your Company 
recorded its highest ever 
revenues of H83,855 crore, 
compared to H76,359 crore in 
FY25, delivering a robust year on 
year growth of 9.8%. Profitability 
strengthened further, with 
EBITDA margins of 12.3%, 
reflecting improved operating 
leverage and disciplined cost 
management. The automotive 
business delivered a return 
on capital employed of 72.3% 
among the highest in the global 
commercial vehicles industry.
Mr. N Chandrasekaran
Chairman 
Dear Shareholders,
It is my privilege to present to you the 
Annual Report of Tata Motors Limited for 
the financial year ended March 31, 2026 
- as a Commercial Vehicles only Company 
following its successful demerger and 
public listing on November 12, 2025. 
This milestone marks a decisive step in our 
ambition to build a world class commercial 
mobility enterprise, with strong leadership 
in India and a significant presence globally. 
I would like to thank all colleagues who 
contributed to the successful execution of 
the demerger and listing.
The year 2026 began with expectations 
of steady global growth, soft inflation and 
easier financial conditions. However, the 
introduction of US tariffs in May 2025 
created significant challenges globally. India responded by reducing its GST 
rates to boost domestic consumption 
which helped prop up domestic growth 
rates in the second half of the year. 
During the year we witnessed positive 
developments including the signing of the 
landmark India-EU trade agreement and 
the interim India-US trade deal. However, 
by early March, the start of the West 
Asia crisis brought rising concerns about 
stagflation—falling output coupled with 
rising inflation.
Fiscal 2026 Performance
In this context, I am pleased to share 
that your Company delivered a robust 
performance in FY26. 
In India, as you are aware, your Company 
has been the undisputed leader in the 
Commercial Vehicles market, due to the enduring strength of our brands, the 
capabilities of our people and customer 
trust earned over decades.
During the year, your Company further 
consolidated this leadership, driven 
by focused product interventions, 
disciplined sales execution and deeper, 
more meaningful customer engagement, 
delivering sales volumes of over 4,35,000 
vehicles, compared to ~3,85,000 vehicles 
in the previous year—representing a 
robust year on year growth of 13%. 
This performance was driven by strong 
momentum across the ‘Intermediate, Light 
and Medium Vehicle (ILMCV)’ and Small 
Commercial Vehicles and Pickups (SCVPU) 
segments. Additionally, we had a notable 
resurgence in our Heavy Commercial 
Vehicle (HCV) Segment, which achieved its 
highest market share to 55% in a decade. 
Chairman’s Message
8
2nd Integrated Annual Report 2025-26
=== page 12 ===
During the year, your Company recorded 
its highest ever revenues of H83,855 
crore, compared to H76,359 crore in 
FY25, delivering a robust year on year 
growth of 9.8%. Profitability strengthened 
further, with EBITDA margins of 12.3%, 
reflecting improved operating leverage 
and disciplined cost management. The 
automotive business delivered a return 
on capital employed of 72.3% among 
the highest in the global commercial 
vehicles industry. Collectively, these 
outcomes highlight the resilience of 
our business model and our ability to 
perform consistently across cycles through 
disciplined execution.
The Board of Directors have 
recommended a final dividend of H4/- 
per share for Fiscal 26, subject to your 
approval.
Fiscal 2026 Progress
Last year, I had shared how your Company 
had organised itself into eight verticals 
to create new revenue streams while 
de-risking the business from economic 
cycles. I am pleased to report that these 
initiatives have translated into strong 
progress during Fiscal 2026. 
The 8-vertical structure has enabled 
sharper focus, accountability and 
improved performance and improved 
profitability. Apart from the 4 vehicular 
segments, we saw strong traction in the 
other 4 segments 
 Non cyclical segment delivered strong 
growth of 18.2% with spares and services 
making a contribution to profitability.
 TML Smart City Mobility Solutions, 
with over 3,800 electric buses 
deployed across 10 cities, surpassed 
the significant milestone of 50 
crore cumulative kilometres while 
consistently delivering uptime above 
95%, demonstrating scale, reliability 
and impact on urban mobility. 
 Digital platforms continued to scale, 
strengthening customer engagement 
and value delivery. Fleet Edge 
crossed the milestone of one million 
connected vehicles while Fleet Verse, 
our digital commerce platform, recorded robust growth across sales, 
bookings and enquiries.
 International Business delivered strong 
year on year growth of 53.9%, driven 
by deeper market penetration and 
notable order wins across Southeast 
Asia, Africa and the Middle East.
During the year, your Company 
announced the proposed acquisition of 
the IVECO Group, an important strategic 
step in our global growth journey. This 
will bring a strong portfolio of light, 
medium and heavy commercial vehicles, 
with operations across European, Latin 
American and other international markets, 
annual sales of approximately ~140,000 
vehicles and revenues of €13.4 billion in 
2025. This will add scale, complementary 
markets, strong manufacturing and 
powertrain capabilities along with a strong 
technology roadmap aligned to evolving 
emission norms and alternative fuel 
powertrains.
The year also saw the Company’s 
continued to focus on renewable energy, 
circular economy and biodiversity. This 
year we progressed towards 100% 
renewable electricity, led the industry’s 
transition with Battery Electric and 
Hydrogen trucks and strengthened 
circularity by bringing several plants 
closer to Water Neutrality and Zero Waste 
to Landfill. We also scaled our ProLife 
and Re.Wi.Re businesses, reinforcing 
responsible vehicle lifecycle management, 
while our biodiversity initiatives - projects 
in the Central Asian Flyway and Maximus 
received global recognition.
Rooted in Tata Group’s enduring values, 
our social investments continued to 
focus on creating sustained, long term 
impact, benefiting over 2 lakh citizens 
across 105 districts. With more than 
30% of beneficiaries from marginalized 
communities, these efforts reaffirm our 
commitment to inclusive and sustainable 
development, spanning key focus areas 
such as water conservation, education, 
skill development and healthcare. 
Further, our flagship Integrated Village 
Development Programme (IVDP) has 
evolved into a scalable model for holistic 
rural transformation, now spanning 194 
villages across five states.Trends Shaping Mobility 
Advances in digital technologies and 
AI are transforming how mobility 
products are designed, experienced and 
supported. The transition to clean energy, 
heightened expectations on safety and the 
reconfiguration of global supply chains are 
redefining competitiveness. Geopolitical 
and uneven economic recovery are adding 
further complexity, making agility and 
resilience as critical capabilities. 
In India, these global shifts are reinforced 
by strong long-term fundamentals. 
Sustained investments in infrastructure, 
logistics modernisation and freight 
efficiency continue to underpin the 
relevance of commercial mobility. 
Looking Ahead
With a strong balance sheet, improving 
returns and focus on resilience, your 
Company is well positioned to sustain 
its profitable growth journey.  Our focus 
will remain on delivering industry leading 
growth, profitability and returns, supported 
by a disciplined capital allocation to 
address emerging mobility trends including 
digital led solutions, connected vehicle 
technologies, advanced driver assistance 
systems, data driven fleet services and 
new age powertrains—capabilities that 
will shape the future of safe, efficient and 
intelligent commercial mobility.
Guided by Project Aalingana, the Tata 
Group’s vision for a greener, cleaner and 
more equitable future, sustainability is 
integral to your Company. The transition 
to cleaner mobility requires a portfolio 
of electric, hydrogen and cleaner ICE 
technologies. While we scale the portfolio 
of zero emission electric CVs, we will 
continue to invest in hydrogen-based 
technologies for heavier-duty segments. 
On behalf of the Board, I would like to 
thank the employees, customers, suppliers 
and shareholders, for your continued trust 
and support.
Warm Regards,
N. Chandrasekaran 
Chairman

FY26 was a defining year for Tata 
Motors Commercial Vehicles. The

MD and CEO’s Letter 
Dear Shareholders,
I hope this letter finds you in good 
health and spirits.
FY26 was a defining year for Tata Motors 
Commercial Vehicles. The successful 
demerger and listing of the Commercial 
Vehicles entity marked more than 
a structural milestone—sharpening 
strategic intent, strengthening 
governance and reinforcing a culture 
of accountability and customer-
centric execution. Operating as 
an independently listed entity is 
enabling clearer capital allocation 
choices, faster decision-making and a deeper alignment between strategy and 
outcomes—true to our promise of Better 
Always.
I am pleased that our Second Annual 
Report as a standalone listed Company 
comes to you at a time when the 
organisation has emerged stronger 
on multiple dimensions – financial, 
operational and organisational. This 
strength has been built deliberately; 
with disciplined execution, resilient 
fundamentals and a clear, action-oriented 
roadmap for sustainable value creation. I 
would like to share the progress we made 
during the year and the principles that will 
continue to guide us.Industry Context 
and Our Response
FY26 unfolded unevenly for the 
domestic commercial vehicle 
industry, with early disruptions 
muting sentiment before a 
decisive recovery in the second 
half. While external factors such 
as supply-chain dislocations 
tested resilience, the industry’s 
rebound was enabled by 
structural enablers including GST 
2.0 implementation, improving 
demand fundamentals and rising 
consumer confidence.
Girish Wagh
Managing Director and 
Chief Executive Officer
10
2nd Integrated Annual Report 2025-26
=== page 14 ===
Our focus during this period was not 
on reacting tactically, but on staying 
anchored to fundamentals—maintaining 
execution discipline, protecting 
customer relationships and aligning 
supply with evolving demand signals. 
This approach allowed us to participate 
meaningfully in the recovery while 
strengthening our competitive position.
Performance Anchored 
in Execution Discipline
Against this backdrop, Tata Motors 
Commercial Vehicles delivered 14% 
(excluding TDM) volume growth 
in FY26. More importantly, this 
performance reflected a shift in 
how we operate—through sharper 
segment-level strategies, clearly defined 
customer value propositions and 
tighter integration between product 
planning, sales execution and supply-
chain readiness. This transformation 
is translating into stronger customer 
advocacy, reflected in sustained gains 
in Net Promoter Scores and overall 
customer satisfaction parameters.
A defining outcome of this approach 
was the HCV Trucks business achieving 
its strongest offtake market share in a 
decade. This was not driven by a single 
intervention, but by sustained, insight-
led actions—aligning products precisely 
to duty cycles, tailoring services to 
address real operating requirements, 
strengthening consultative selling and 
engaging customers through deeper 
insights into their operating economics 
with Fleet Edge.
Towards the end of the year, 
geopolitical developments in West Asia 
introduced supply-side disruptions and 
moderated activity in select sectors. 
Our response once again underscored 
how resilience is built—through cross 
functional coordination across sourcing, 
manufacturing and sales, calibrated 
demand-supply alignment and proactive, on-ground customer engagement. 
Supporting customers through tailored 
solutions during this period reaffirmed the 
robustness of our operating model and 
the agility of our organisation.
Strengthening Financial 
Fitness Prudently
Profitability improvement remained 
intentional and structured. Rather 
than pursuing growth for its own sake, 
we embedded financial fitness into 
decision-making across the business. 
Mix improvement, disciplined cost 
governance and a sharper capital 
allocation framework ensured that every 
growth lever was evaluated through the 
lens of returns and cash generation.
Better realisations, rigorous fixed-cost 
control and a growing contribution 
from relatively non-cyclical businesses 
improved the quality of earnings. These 
were reinforced by systematic working 
capital discipline and tighter cash 
controls across the value chain. 
As a result, FY26 marked a milestone 
year—with improved revenues and 
profits, robust margins and healthy 
cash flows. These outcomes reflect 
not only strong market participation, 
but consistency of execution and the 
inherent resilience of our business 
model across cycles.
Product Leadership 
Built Around Customer 
Economics
Product leadership during the year was 
shaped by a clear conviction: 
lowering the total cost of ownership 
across the vehicle lifecycle. Our teams 
focused on modular platforms to 
enable speed and scale, strengthened 
application-led design capabilities and 
adapted new technologies for Indian 
operating conditions.The launch of Ace Pro—India’s most 
affordable four wheeler mini truck—was 
anchored in this thinking, addressing 
the ownership economics of small 
entrepreneurs and first time business 
owners. The introduction of 17 next 
generation trucks and tippers reflected 
deeper customer co creation and 
sharper segmentation, setting new 
benchmarks in safety, efficiency  
and profitability.
A landmark step was the upgrade of 
truck cabins to meet European safety 
regulations—a deliberate investment 
that raises industry standards while 
strengthening long-term customer trust 
and brand credibility.
Building New Growth 
Engines with Discipline
Beyond core vehicles, we continued to 
scale adjacencies through a measured, 
outcome led approach. Parts and 
Services sustained their multi year 
growth trajectory, while new businesses 
such as Automotive Fluids, Aggregates 
and FleetCare were scaled with clear 
customer value and profitability lenses.
International Business performance 
improved through a disciplined focus 
on local partnerships, tailored products 
and risk calibrated market expansion 
across more than 40 countries.
Through TML Smart City Mobility 
Solutions, over 3,800 electric buses 
were deployed across 10+ cities—
enabled by integrated planning covering 
charging infrastructure, fleet uptime 
and operational excellence. These 
deployments illustrate how thoughtful 
system-level execution translates 
into dependable public transport and 
tangible societal benefits.
In the digital domain, FleetEdge—
now with over one million connected 
vehicles—demonstrates the power 
of data driven value propositions. AI

Embedding Safety 
and Sustainability in 
Operating Decisions
Safety is now more deeply ingrained 
across our ecosystem, with greater 
consistency in how it is practiced and 
extending beyond our own operations 
to business partners, bus depots and 
dealer workshops, driving higher 
discipline and accountability at 
every touchpoint.
This integrated approach is equally 
reflected in how we are advancing 
sustainability. It is not treated as a 
parallel agenda, but as a core element 
of building a future-ready business. 
Under Project Aalingana, we have 
accelerated progress across Net Zero 
GHG emissions, Circular Economy and 
Biodiversity through clearly defined 
targets, strong operating ownership and 
focused on-ground execution.
Alongside advances towards renewable 
electricity, our product portfolio 
transformation continues through EVs, 
alternative fuels and pioneering rollouts

Strategic and Performance Review
The fiscal 2026 was a year of strong performance for Tata Motors. The business delivered 
growth in volumes, revenue and profitability, reinforcing its position in the domestic market 
while also making progress on its international ambitions. This performance was achieved 
through disciplined execution, a focused product programme and the continued deepening 
of digital and downstream capabilities.
Financial Performance
The business delivered healthy financial 
results in FY26, with revenue, margins 
and profitability all improving over 
the prior year. Strong operational 
performance was complemented by 
efficient working capital management, 
enabling the business to generate 
robust free cash flow and further 
strengthen its balance sheet. Return 
on capital employed (ROCE) improved 
year on year, reflecting the benefits 
of sustained financial discipline and 
improving business quality over time.
Growth was driven not only by higher 
volumes but also by a focus on 
improving realisations through a better 
product mix, managing costs through 
a challenging commodity environment 
and growing the contribution of 
downstream and services businesses 
that provide greater earnings stability 
through the cycle.Strengthening Market 
Leadership
The business maintained its leadership 
position across the domestic 
commercial vehicles market, with 
market share holding firm across trucks, 
buses and passenger carriers. In the 
heavy commercial vehicle segment, 
the business strengthened its position 
over the course of the year, reflecting 
sustained customer preference and 
competitive product performance.
A significant product programme 
supported this outcome. New truck 
launches, the introduction of new 
product ranges and the upgrade of 
the portfolio to meet enhanced safety 
standards all contributed to deepening 
the business's presence across 
segments and improving the overall 
value proposition for customers.Growing the 
International Business
The international business delivered a 
strong performance in FY26, with export 
volumes growing meaningfully year on 
year. The business secured significant 
new orders for international markets 
and continued to develop its presence 
across geographies. This diversification 
beyond the domestic market adds 
resilience to the overall business and 
reflects the growing competitiveness of 
the portfolio on a global stage.
The business remains attentive to 
geopolitical developments that may 
affect specific markets and corridors 
in the near term and has taken steps 
to manage associated risks while 
continuing to pursue international 
growth opportunities.
Advancing Sustainability
Progress on sustainability continued 
across all three pillars of the Company's 
agenda in FY26. Scope 3 emissions 
declined for the second consecutive 
year and renewable energy penetration 
in CV operations continued to grow, 
keeping the business on track towards 
its longer term Net Zero and RE100 
goals. Several manufacturing plants 
reached important milestones in water 
neutrality and zero waste-to-landfill, 
reflecting the depth of sustainability 
practices embedded across operations.
The circular economy programme 
expanded further through the growth of 
registered vehicle scrappage facilities, 
reinforcing the Company's commitment 
to responsible end-of-life vehicle 
management. Employee engagement in 
sustainability initiatives also continued 
to deepen across the organisation.

Product and Technology 
Leadership
Investment in future technologies 
continued at pace in FY26. The 
Company expanded its electric vehicle 
portfolio across buses, trucks and small 
commercial vehicles, with EV adoption 
growing on the back of improving 
economics and supportive policy. 
The portfolio now spans a wide  
range of applications, from last-mile 
delivery to heavy-duty haulage and 
public transport.
Progress on alternate fuel technologies 
also advanced, with pilot deployments 
of hydrogen-powered trucks on select 
freight corridors representing an 
important step in the Company's clean 
mobility agenda. Work with ecosystem 
partners to build the infrastructure 
necessary for wider adoption of 
hydrogen continues. In bus mobility, 
meaningful orders from state transport 
undertakings during the year reflected 
continued confidence in the Company's 
bus portfolio.
Expanding Downstream 
Opportunities
The downstream business continued 
to deliver consistent growth, driven by 
higher spares and service penetration 
across the customer base. At the same 
time, our digital platforms strengthened 
market reach and customer engagement 
across genuine parts, automotive fluids 
and fleet care solutions. The growing 
contribution of downstream earnings 
to overall profitability provides the 
business with greater resilience through 
the vehicle volume cycle and reflects 
the value of the long-term customer 
relationships that the business has built 
over time.
Digital and Ecosystem 
Capabilities
The Company's digital platforms 
continued to scale in FY26. The Fleet 
Edge telematics platform expanded its connected vehicle base and its fuel 
efficiency tools delivered measurable 
improvements for fleet operators. 
Fleet Verse, the digital marketplace for 
commercial vehicle transactions, grew 
its user base and saw an increasing 
share of total retail business transacted 
through the platform.
In manufacturing, Industry 4.0 
deployment continued to advance 
across plants, with improvements in 
connected manufacturing, equipment 
monitoring, safety systems and supply 
chain visibility. Building the capability 
of the workforce to work alongside 
these technologies remained a priority 
through the year.
The ecosystem play extended beyond 
the vehicle itself, encompassing 
charging infrastructure for electric 
fleets, financial partnerships to 
improve access to fleet financing and 
collaboration with fuel and logistics 
partners. These efforts together 
support the Company's aim of being 
a comprehensive mobility solutions 
provider rather than simply a  
vehicle manufacturer.
Managing Costs
Commodity costs presented a headwind 
during the year. The business responded through a combination of selective 
pricing actions and a focused cost 
management programme spanning 
procurement, manufacturing efficiency 
and value engineering. The approach 
was calibrated to protect customer 
affordability and sustain demand 
momentum, reflecting the business's 
view that long-term customer 
relationships are a core asset to be 
preserved through periods  
of cost pressure.
Outlook
The business enters FY27 with sound 
fundamentals and a competitive 
portfolio. Industry growth is expected 
to be more moderate than in FY26, 
reflecting a higher base and some 
near-term uncertainties in the external 
environment. The underlying demand 
drivers for commercial vehicles in India 
remain constructive, supported by 
infrastructure activity, improving fleet 
utilisation and the ongoing transition 
towards cleaner and more connected 
transport. The business is well placed 
to navigate near-term challenges while 
continuing to invest in the capabilities 
and technologies that will sustain its 
competitiveness over the longer term.

External Environment
FY26 was a year of two distinct halves for the commercial vehicle industry. The first half 
remained subdued, weighed down by cautious customer sentiment and a slow start to 
infrastructure execution. The second half saw a decisive recovery as demand conditions 
improved with the rollout of GST 2.0 and momentum built steadily through Q3 and Q4 as 
freight activity picked up and customer confidence returned.
Against this backdrop, Tata Motors delivered broad-based growth across product lines, 
customer segments and markets. The business strengthened its competitive position 
through improved realisations, disciplined cost management and targeted portfolio 
actions through the year.
Demand Recovery and 
Quarterly Trends
Industry volumes remained soft 
through the first half but recovered 
meaningfully as the year progressed. Q3 
saw sequential improvement driven by 
a pickup in infrastructure activity and 
festive season demand and Q4 closed 
with particular strength — registering 
the highest quarterly volumes in several 
years. The recovery was broad-based, 
with growth spread across heavy and 
medium trucks, passenger carriers and 
small commercial vehicles.
Towards the end of the year, monthly 
growth saw some moderation, partly 
attributable to the ongoing conflict 
in West Asia and its impact on select 
sectors of the economy. The business 
responded proactively, intensifying 
efforts to support customers in 
managing emerging operating 
challenges and ensuring  
logistics continuity.
Freight Environment and 
Customer Sentiment
Improving freight availability and 
stronger fleet economics were central 
to the demand recovery in the second 
half. Consistent growth in e-way bill 
generation reflected the underlying 
health of goods movement across 
the Indian economy, reinforcing the 
structural demand for commercial vehicles. Fleet operators, who had been 
cautious earlier in the year, returned 
to buying with greater conviction 
in H2, supported by stable interest 
rates, manageable fuel prices and low 
financing delinquencies.
Exports and 
International Markets
The international business was a 
standout performer in FY26, with 
export volumes posting significant 
year-on-year growth driven by large 
international orders and focused market 
development efforts. This diversification 
beyond the domestic cycle added 
meaningful resilience to overall volume 
performance. However, the conflict in 
West Asia began to affect sentiment in 
certain export markets, particularly in 
North Africa and the Middle East and 
the business has been actively assessing 
the risk landscape and putting in place 
appropriate mitigation measures to 
manage potential disruption  
to select corridors.
Product and Portfolio 
Actions
Tata Motors strengthened its 
competitive position through a 
significant product year. New launches 
included the Ace Pro and Winger 9S, 
the entire truck range was upgraded 
to meet European safety norms and 
the new Azura range was introduced. These actions deepened the Company’s 
presence across key segments and 
sharpened its value proposition for 
customers. A broader programme of 
next-generation truck launches through 
the year was aimed at refreshing and 
future-proofing the portfolio ahead 
of evolving customer and regulatory 
requirements.
Electric and Alternate 
Fuel Momentum
Electric commercial vehicles continued 
to gain meaningful traction in FY26, 
with EV volumes posting strong year-on-
year growth. Growth was led by buses 
and small commercial vehicles, where 
improving total cost of ownership 
economics and supportive government 
policies accelerated adoption. The 
Company expanded its electric CV 
portfolio across buses, trucks and small 
commercial vehicles during the year, 
investing ahead of time in EV hardware 
and control software to enhance the 
performance and range of its  
electric products.
The Company also progressed its 
hydrogen roadmap in FY26, with pilot 
deployments of hydrogen-powered 
trucks underway on select freight 
corridors. This marks a significant 
milestone in the Company’s alternate 
fuel agenda and reflects its commitment 
to offering customers a range of 
sustainable choices across energy types.

Commodity and Cost 
Environment
Commodity costs emerged as a key 
area of concern during the latter 
part of the year and into FY27. Rising 
prices of steel, aluminium and copper 
exerted increasing pressure on input 
costs, requiring disciplined cost 
management and operational efficiency 
measures. The business implemented 
a measured price increase to partially 
offset these pressures, while being 
mindful of the importance of protecting 
customer affordability and domestic 
sales momentum. Disciplined cost 
management, pricing actions and 
product mix improvement were the 
key levers deployed to protect margins 
through the year.
Diesel prices remain a key monitorable, 
given their significant role in the total 
cost of ownership for fleet operators. 
Any sustained rise in fuel prices has a 
direct bearing on fleet economics and 
can temper buying decisions  
across the industry.
FY27 Key Priorities
The commercial vehicle industry 
is expected to sustain its growth 
trajectory in FY27, albeit at a more 
moderate pace, reflecting a strong base 
from FY26 and near-term headwinds 
including commodity cost pressure, 
geopolitical uncertainty and potential 
demand implications of new regulatory 
requirements. The business remains agile and is closely tracking 
geopolitical developments and the 
evolving macro environment.
Priorities for FY27 include scaling the 
refreshed product portfolio, sustaining 
profitable growth across segments, 
expanding electric and sustainable 
mobility offerings, growing international 
business while navigating geopolitical 
risks and maintaining cost discipline and 
capital efficiency. With a comprehensive 
and future-ready product range 
supported by smart digital solutions, 
Tata Motors is well positioned to 
capture emerging opportunities and 
deliver sustained value to its customers 
and all stakeholders.

The demerger of the Commercial Vehicles business was completed last year, empowering 
Tata Motors to pursue strategies that deliver higher growths with greater agility while 
reinforcing accountability. The operating environment in which we operate, continues 
to be shaped by heightened competitive intensity, rapid technological evolution and an 
increasing regulatory framework spanning emissions, safety and sustainability.
Tata Motors’ long-standing leadership, comprehensive product portfolio, strong 
distribution reach and deep understanding of markets place it in a position of strength. 
A disciplined demand-led approach, sustained investments in engineering, productivity 
and digital capabilities, enables Tata Motors to compete effectively while protecting 
margins and driving long-term value creation.
Domestic Demand Scenario
India’s macroeconomic environment remained supportive during the year, anchored by strong domestic fundamentals. Real 
GDP grew by 7.6% in FY26, driven by resilient consumption and steady investment momentum. Government spending is key 
in shaping freight demand. The Union Budget for FY27 has proposed a capital expenditure outlay of H12.22 lakh crore, up from 
H11.21 lakh crore in FY26. This sustained focus on infrastructure is expected to support construction, mining and logistics activity, 
directly benefiting core CV segments and improving medium-term demand visibility.
The CV industry delivered a strong performance in FY26, recording its highest ever annual volumes of 10.79 lakh units, a growth 
of 12.6% over last year, surpassing the earlier peak of FY19. The year saw a tale of two halves— the first half was impacted by 
early monsoons and cautious fleet sentiment, demand rebounded sharply in the second half. Key enablers included the rollout of 
GST 2.0, RBI repo rate cuts, firmer freight rates, higher e-commerce-led logistics movement and renewed infrastructure activity. 
Improved financing conditions, with better returns and lower NPAs, further strengthened fleet operators’ buying confidence.

Implications for the Business

Connected Vehicles, Electrification

Connected CVs are becoming industry

in fleet efficiency, uptime and asset

enabling real-time vehicle health

global OEMs offering this digital service

Tata Motors is committed to achieving 
net zero emissions by 2045, supported

Company follows a multi pathway 
decarbonisation strategy, offering 
solutions across diesel, CNG, 
battery electric, LNG and hydrogen 
technologies. Electrification is gaining

and applications. The Company 
has established one of India’s most 
comprehensive electric commercial 
vehicle portfolios across segments, 
ranging from sub-1-tonne to 55-tonne ADAS, electrification, connectivity and software-defined mobility are transforming the commercial vehicle industry at an 
accelerating pace. The growth in software-define vehicles (SDV) reflects a structural shift in the automotive value chain from 
hardware-led development to scalable, recurring, software-driven revenues enabled by OTA updates and subscription-based 
services. SDVs transform commercial vehicles into upgradeable platforms, enhancing uptime, efficiency and lifetime value. 
Increasing adoption of software-centric architectures, particularly in commercial vehicles, signals a move towards integrated, 
service-oriented mobility platforms delivering higher lifecycle value to customers.

mobility is expected to accelerate, with increasing adoption of software-centric

Sustainability and ESG Focus
Implications for the Business
 ESG imperatives influence product 
development, operations and 
regulatory compliance
 Increasing focus on  
decarbonisation, resource efficiency 
and circularity shapes long-term 
business sustainability.Our Strategic Response
Tata Motors places sustainability 
and ESG principles at the core of its 
strategy and operations. Aligned with 
the Tata Group’s Project Aalingana, the 
Company pursues responsible growth 
by balancing economic performance 
with environmental stewardship, social 
responsibility and strong governance—
building long-term resilience in a rapidly 
evolving mobility ecosystem.
Tata Motors has defined a roadmap 
to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas 
emissions by 2045 and a commitment to 
transition to 100% renewable electricity 
by 2030. In FY26, renewable electricity 
accounted for approximately 51% of

Global economic and geopolitical environment
We operate in a highly dynamic 
and increasingly complex global 
environment marked by political 
shifts, economic volatility, trade 
tensions, tariff disruptions, 
regional conflicts and climate-
related challenges. The ongoing 
realignment of the global trade 
landscape, including higher 
tariffs and bilateral trade 
restrictions, poses direct risks 
to supply chains, commodity 
availability and demand 
patterns across markets.India continues to be Tata Motors’ primary 
market, supported by strong economic 
fundamentals. Domestic demand remains 
closely linked to infrastructure spending, 
growth in logistics and mining activity and 
government capital expenditure cycles. 
However, global geopolitical conflicts 
may impact the domestic market through 
demand slowdown, fiscal tightening or 
policy changes, potentially affecting industry 
volumes.
Our export footprint is expanding across 
SAARC, Sub-Saharan Africa, North Africa, 
the Middle East and ASEAN. These 
regions remain sensitive to geopolitical 
developments, currency volatility and 
changes in import regulations, which may 
influence demand stability.
In addition, rising global tariff barriers and 
environmental regulations, such as the 
Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism 
(CBAM), could increase cross-border 
sourcing costs, elevate raw material prices 
and impact the competitiveness of exports.We remain agile in continuously assessing the 
risk landscape, with a sharp focus on geopolitical 
developments and the evolving macroeconomic-
environment. We closely track macroeconomic 
trends and projections to understand the forces 
shaping the economy and the automotive industry. 
Appropriate mitigation measures are implemented 
to strengthen organisational resilience and ensure 
production continuity. Risks arising from geopolitical 
developments are reviewed through our Risk 
Management Framework.
Our diversified domestic portfolio provides a natural 
hedge against segment-specific demand cycles. 
Disciplined cost management through material 
cost optimisation, value engineering, localisation 
initiatives and calibrated pricing actions ensures 
financial fitness without compromising competitive 
positioning or customer centricity.
We also engage proactively with government 
stakeholders and industry bodies on tariff policy, 
infrastructure planning and sector-specific fiscal 
measures to anticipate change and identify future 
growth opportunities.Context Implications Response

Supply chain disruptions and commodity price fluctuations
Automotive OEMs require a broad 
spectrum of raw materials and 
commodities, including steel, 
aluminium, copper, rubber, plastics, 
precious metals and rare earth 
elements, to produce a wide range 
of vehicles. These inputs constitute a 
significant proportion of total vehicle 
cost and their prices are subject to 
volatility arising from global market 
conditions, geopolitical disruptions, 
energy cost movements, exchange 
rate fluctuations and tariff dynamics.
In addition, the increasing 
electrification and digitalisation 
of our portfolio are introducing 
new supply chain dependencies. 
Critical inputs such as battery cells, 
semiconductors, lithium and other 
EV-related minerals are becoming 
increasingly important, each carrying 
distinct availability risks, supply 
concentration challenges and 
cost structures that could impact 
production continuity and margins.We leverage long-standing strategic relationships 
with key suppliers to proactively identify emerging 
supply chain risks, dynamically re-route logistics 
and develop alternate sourcing solutions to ensure 
uninterrupted production. Strategic inventory 
buffers are maintained for critical components to 
safeguard production continuity against short-term 
supply disruptions.
Financial risk management practices, including 
the use of forward contracts and options for key 
commodity exposures, are deployed to mitigate 
short-term price volatility and enhance planning 
certainty. Long-term supply agreements are entered 
into with key suppliers for critical commodities and 
sub-assemblies, ensuring price visibility, supply 
assurance and improved cost predictability.
Value Analysis and Value Engineering (VAVE) is 
an institutionalised and continuous programme 
focused on improving product cost structures, 
thereby reducing and mitigating the impact  
of cost inflation.
Additionally, effective collaboration within the Tata 
Group and with strategic suppliers is accelerating 
localisation initiatives, reducing import dependence 
and strengthening supply chain resilience for EV-
critical components.Context
Sustained increases in the prices 
of key commodities such as steel, 
aluminium and copper can put 
pressure on margins unless offset 
through timely pricing actions or 
structural cost-reduction programmes. 
Given the highly competitive nature 
of the commercial vehicle industry, 
the ability to pass through input cost 
inflation through price increases 
remains constrained.
Supply chain bottlenecks across 
critical aggregates and components 
may limit production throughput and 
deliveries, with direct implications for 
revenue realisation, order fulfilment 
timelines and customer satisfaction.
Moreover, the electrification of 
commercial vehicles is creating 
new and increasingly concentrated 
supply chain dependencies. Limited 
domestic manufacturing capabilities 
for EV-critical components increase 
import dependence, exposing us 
to geopolitical supply disruptions, 
availability constraints and heightened 
price volatility.Implications Response04

IT systems, security and data management
With advanced telematics enabling 
seamless connectivity features and 
increasing electronic content across 
multiple aggregates, vehicles are 
becoming a significant source of data. 
While this presents value-creation 
opportunities for various stakeholders, 
the data must be protected from 
unauthorised access and misuse.
The ever-increasing threat of 
cybercrime, including ransomware 
attacks and data exfiltration, 
poses material risks to system 
availability, data integrity and 
confidentiality. Simultaneously, 
the Indian regulatory landscape 
has undergone a fundamental shift 
with the notification of the Digital 
Personal Data Protection (DPDP) 
Rules, creating new time-bound 
compliance obligations for 
data fiduciaries.
Managing the growing complexity of IT 
systems, including legacy infrastructure 
migration, further elevates this as a 
high-priority enterprise risk.IT systems, cybersecurity and 
data governance have become 
foundational to Tata Motors’ 
operations, spanning manufacturing 
processes, engineering design and 
our rapidly expanding portfolio of 
connected commercial vehicles. 
These systems collectively handle 
significant volumes of sensitive fleet, 
customer and operational data.
A severe ransomware attack or 
targeted cyber intrusion could cause 
significant production disruptions, 
vehicle delivery delays and direct 
revenue loss.
Unauthorised access to, or exfiltration 
of, data related to connected 
vehicle platforms could constitute 
a serious breach of customer trust 
and may result in significant loss of 
competitive advantage
Further, the notification of India’s 
Digital Personal Data Protection 
(DPDP) Rules in November 2025, 
with full compliance obligations 
effective from May 2027, introduces 
material regulatory exposure. 
Non-compliance, including failure 
to implement consent-based data 
processing and breach notification 
obligations, could result in  
significant penalties.Information risk and cybersecurity are managed 
strategically through a cohesive enterprise programme 
with structured review mechanisms across multiple levels, 
including Senior Management. Our IT security framework 
is aligned with international cybersecurity standards and 
integrates proven industry practices, while continuously 
adapting to evolving regulatory requirements.
Our IT infrastructure is regularly assessed by leading 
external cybersecurity firms through planned internal 
and external audits. Comprehensive access logs are 
maintained to detect and investigate unauthorised 
activity. We actively collaborate with industry experts and 
ethical security researchers to identify and remediate 
vulnerabilities through responsible disclosure processes.
Connected vehicle cybersecurity is embedded across 
the product development lifecycle. Security testing is 
integrated at the design stage for all connected features, 
platform updates and Firmware Over-The-Air (FOTA)-
capable vehicle systems, ensuring that over-the-air update 
channels are authenticated, encrypted and protected 
against unauthorised firmware injection.
We have adopted a comprehensive roadmap to ensure 
compliance with the DPDP Act and DPDP Rules, with 
structured programmes involving relevant stakeholders 
across functions.
Employee awareness programmes, role-specific 
cybersecurity training and regular simulation exercises—
including phishing and ransomware scenario drills—form 
a critical layer of defence, reducing the risk of human-
factor security breaches.Context Implications Response05

 While safety is the core foundation for

develop advanced technologies that 
strengthen integrated safety including 
both active and passive safety. As EVs 
redefine the future of trucking, we have 
embedded safety at the core of our EV 
products. The EV products incorporate 
industry leading safety features across 
high voltage (HV) systems, vehicle 
architecture and software, including HV 
interlock loops, over current and over/
under voltage protection, thermal and 
battery thermal runaway protection, 
along with multiple visual indicators 
and warning systems. These systems 
also enable automated isolation and 
shutdown of HV systems in the event of 
an accident. As total cost of ownership (TCO) has 
evolved as a critical decision driving 
criteria for customers, our focus has 
been on developing TCO enhancement 
technologies and delivering best-in-
class TCO across platforms and vehicle 
architectures. Our circularity -driven

re-refined oil, exploring water borne 
paints, use of recycled steel, recovered 
carbon black and simplified emission 
architectures, supported by our broader 
circularity objectives. These efforts 
resulted in considerable reduction 
in overall CO₂ emissions, improving 
circularity in design, while strengthening 
preparedness for future regulatory 
and sustainability requirements. 
Collectively, these initiatives support 
cost-effective innovation and reinforce 
compliance, operational efficiency and 
environmental performance. 
 We also made significant progress in

organizational readiness and ecosystem

customer -centric featured roadmap

across commercial vehicle segments. 
 We are progressively adopting

Future Areas  
of Focus: E
Going forward, our R&D engineering efforts will 
increasingly be oriented toward enabling global 
growth through differentiated, locally relevant 
technology solutions. We will focus on developing 
adaptable platforms and architectures that address 
diverse regulatory, operating and customer 
requirements across international markets, rather 
than pursuing a one-size-fits-all replication. 
Going forward, material innovation will remain a critical 
focus area as the industry accelerates the transition 
toward electrification and alternative energy solutions. 
We will continue to advance research in next -generation 
battery technologies, including solid-state systems, 
supported by the development of advanced thermal 
management materials and lightweight enclosures to 
enhance vehicle range, safety and cost efficiency in 
electric commercial vehicles. 
While regulatory frameworks will continue to shape the 
commercial vehicle landscape, the future direction of our 
R&D efforts is anchored in building technology-driven 
leadership. Our focus will extend beyond compliance to 
proactively shape solutions that advance green mobility, 
enhance vehicle safety and improve operational efficiency. 
Strategic investments in electrification, hydrogen mobility 
and energy-optimized systems will be complemented 
by initiatives to reduce total cost of ownership through 
intelligent design and lifecycle optimization. At the same 
time, we will accelerate the transition toward software-
defined vehicles and connected platforms, enabling 
smarter, safer and more responsive solutions. Together, 
these efforts will strengthen our long term competitiveness 
and enable us to be ‘Better Always’ as a leader in future-
ready, sustainable mobility.We will emphasize early-stage market and technology 
assessment, modular design philosophies and deeper 
collaboration with global and local partners to accelerate 
innovation. Our structured engineering strategy, supported 
by clear governance frameworks and scalable development 
models, will guide the transition from concept definition to 
execution, ensuring that global expansion is achieved in a 
technologically robust, sustainable and efficient manner. 
In parallel to EVs, we will intensify our efforts in hydrogen-
based mobility solutions for long haul applications using 
composite storage tanks, specialised fuel cell materials and 
advanced metal hydrides. Future development will also 
increasingly leverage smart and functional materials—such 
as self-healing coatings, embedded sensors and phase 
change materials—to improve durability, enhance safety 
and enable predictive maintenance across vehicle platforms, 
supporting sustainable and resilient mobility solutions.

and positioning it as a leader in sustainable maritime infrastructure.

Circularity through Design
We are advancing circularity across our 
vehicle portfolio by embedding Design 
for Circularity principles that prioritise 
recyclability, ease of dismantling 
and sustainable material selection. 
These considerations are integrated 
at the earliest stages of product 
development, with our engineering 
teams incorporating circularity into 
vehicle architecture, material choices 
and component design to minimise 
environmental impact across the 
product lifecycle.
Design for Disassembly (DfD) is a critical 
element of this app roach. Vehicles are 
developed using modular architectures 
that allow easier removal and replacement of major aggregates. 
The use of standardised fasteners and 
clear material separation improves 
recyclability and facilitates efficient 
recovery of materials at end of a 
vehicle’s life.
Material circularity is further 
strengthened through
 Increased use of recyclable metals 
such as steel and aluminium
 Adoption of recyclable 
thermoplastics
 Avoidance of multi material bonded 
components, wherever feasible, to 
simplify dismantling and recycling
 Progressive reduction of hazardous 
materials in line with End-of-Life 
Vehicle (ELV) regulations, supporting 
Circularity Initiatives Across 
the Vehicle Lifecycle
At the manufacturing stage, we focus on 
improving resource efficiency through 
process optimisation and material 
management. Key initiatives include 
material yield improvement in press 
shops, closed loop recycling of steel and 
aluminium scrap and systematic reuse 
of process scrap. Our initiatives include 
Tata Motors Prolife has been a leading 
example of the circular economy in 
action for over 25 years.
It is a pioneering aftermarket support 
initiative which aims to remanufacture 
old and used vehicle aggregates 
to factory standards for delivering 
original equipment-level performance 
and extending the vehicle life. Prolife 
embraces a circular approach centred 
on ‘Take–Make–Reuse’, creating 
positive environmental and social 
outcomes while promoting more 
sustainable consumption of resources.
End-of-life components are reclaimed 
and rebuilt through innovative Product Lifetime  
Extension through
ProLifesalvaging processes and precision re-
machining processes. This enables the 
reuse of valuable parts, supporting 
greater component circularity and 
reducing the need to manufacture 
new parts from virgin raw materials. 
As a result, we conserve resources, 
minimise waste and contribute 
meaningfully to environmental 
sustainability. Tata Motors Prolife 
remanufactures entire range of engine 
long blocks fitted on Tata Motors 
Commercial vehicles with emission 
compliance norms ranging from BSI 
to BSVI.
Beyond engines, the Prolife portfolio 
also includes clutch assemblies, 
cabins, after-treatment systems and 
fuel injection equipment, extending 
the benefits of circularity across 
multiple vehicle systems.as a central lever for improving carbon 
efficiency across our supply chain.
We are also working closely with

remanufacturing wherever feasible,

Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs)
In lin e with our sustainability strategy, 
we undertake comprehensive Life Cycle 
Assessments (LCAs) to evaluate the 
environmental impacts of our products 
across the entire value chain, from raw 
material extraction and manufacturing 
through vehicle use and end-of-life 
management. These assessments 
consider resource consumption, 
environmental impacts such as 
greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and 
ecotoxicity, as well as potential impacts 
on human health, including human 
toxicity and ionising radiation.
We assess environmental performance 
using internationally recognised 
indicators, including global warming 
potential, acidification potential and  
eutrophication potential.
To date, we have conducted cradle-
to-gate LCA assessments for multiple 
commercial vehicle models, including 
the Magic Bi Fuel (passenger van), Ultra 
T.7 (ILCV truck), Signa 5530.S (tractor 
trailer vehicle) and LPO11.6 bus chassis.
These studies provide valuable insights 
into environmental impact hotspots 
across materials and processes,  
helping us identify opportunities for 
targeted improvement.The findings support data-driven actions 
to
 Reduce product carbon footprint
 Optimise resource efficiency
 Minimise waste generation
 Increase the adoption of sustainable 
materials
These learnings are systematically 
integrated into our product 
development and engineering processes 
through defined decarbonisation 
pathways and material circularity 
targets, reinforcing our Design for 
Circularity approach for future 
commercial vehicle platforms.

Waste Management

sustainable waste management, supported 
by a robust internal auditing mechanism 
that enables the systematic identification, 
classification and monitoring of waste

hazardous based on its characteristics.
Across our operations, we implement 
focused initiatives aimed at eliminating, 
minimising and recycling waste, in full 
compliance with statutory requirements 
and aligned with identified opportunities. 
These efforts are guided by clearly defined 
targets that are cascaded across individual 
operational sites, ensuring accountability 
and consistent performance.
Our waste management approach includes 
material recovery through authorised 
recyclers, co-processing of hazardous 
waste as an alternative fuel and raw 
material source and the recycling of 
both metal and non-metal scrap through 
approved channels.Driving circularity

Water Stewardship
We recognise water as a shared, finite 
and critical natural resource and are 
committed to its responsible and 
sustainable management. To support 
this commitment, we have implemented 
a comprehensive internal auditing 
framework that systematically tracks and 
categorises water based on withdrawal 
sources, including surface water, 
groundwater and third-party supplies, as 
well as discharge destinations.
We focus on optimising water use 
through a judicious combination of 
water conservation measures, effluent 
recycling and process usage and 
rainwater harvesting and usage, tailored 
to prevailing conditions at each plant 
location. These sustained efforts have 
resulted in a 7% reduction in specific 
operational water withdrawal per vehicle, 
reflecting ongoing improvements in water 
efficiency across our operations.
We further reinforce our water 
management programme through 
employee training and awareness 
initiatives, the adoption of advanced 
technologies, enhanced monitoring 
and analytical tools and the proactive 
identification of opportunities to reduce 
water consumption and prevent wastage. 
Together, these measures are supporting 
all our plants in progressing towards 
our Water Positive ambition by 2030, 
reaffirming our commitment to  
long-term water stewardship and 
environmental sustainability.Use of Treated External 
Sewage Water for Plant 
Process RequirementsAt the Jamshedpur Tata Motors

capacity of 1.6 MLD has been 
established, along with a 1 MLD 
tertiary treatment Ultra Filter and 
Reverse Osmosis (UF & RO) plant. 
Operational since January 2026, 
the facility supplies treated water 
for process requirements at 
Jamshedpur Works, enabling an 
equivalent reduction in freshwater 
consumption and supporting our 
commitment to sustainable  
water stewardshi p.

is expected to reduce freshwater

KLD annually. 
Together, these initiatives demonstrate 
how circular economy principles 
can be applied to advance our

repurposing treated external

Preserving Nature and Biodiversity
TML’s biodiversity strategy is aligned 
with the Group’s Aalingana strategy, 
metrics and milestones and provides a 
structured roadmap for delivering a Net 
Positive Impact on biodiversity. At an 
enterprise level, the strategy outlines 
actions to restore, enhance and protect 
nature, ensuring that our activities 
contribute positively to biodiversity 
outcomes over the long term.
Our biodiversity journey began with 
active engagement between senior 
leadership and leading subject matter 
experts and conservation practitioners.

Own Operations
Since inception, all our operational 
sites in India have designated dedicated 
areas for the development of greenbelts 
and wetlands, reflecting our long-
standing commitment to biodiversity 
conservation. A comprehensive 
biodiversity baseline survey across all 
TML Plants was conducted out to get 
an in-depth understanding of floristic 
and faunal diversity, extent of threats, 
presence of species with special 
conservation value and other challenges. 
Building on this foundation, we 
undertook LiDAR-based drone surveys 
to map habitats, contours, surface water 
flows and other critical geographical 
features required for effective ecosystem 
restoration planning.
At our Pimpri Lakehouse Area in Pune, 
we developed a comprehensive eco-
restoration master plan supported by 
robust scientific metrics. The first phase of implementation, covering 141 acres, 
was initiated in FY26 with the objective 
of delivering measurable improvements 
in biodiversity and ecosystem services. 
Drawing on the learnings from this 
pilot, we are developing ecosystem 
restoration plans for all our Commercial 
Vehicle locations during FY26, with 
implementation scheduled for the 
following year. The eco-restoration 
projects are structured to meet the 
criteria laid down in the MoEFCC-NBA-
UNDP backed OECM framework (i.e. 
Other Effective Area Based Conservation 
Measures) – which expands the scope 
of area-based conservation beyond 
legally protected areas. These Tata 
Motors ‘nature hot-spots’ set in the 
midst of industrial estates, will serve 
as a lighthouse of best practice in 
biodiversity conservation. We are also 
actively engaging employees and local 
stakeholders throughout this journey, 
fostering awareness, supporting 
research and encouraging wider adoption of conservation practices to 
create positive impacts that extend well 
beyond our operational boundaries. 
Value Chain
Automobile manufacturing sources a 
diverse range of parts, materials and 
consumables from a complex global 
supply chain. This sourcing determines 
the level of both dependency and 
impact on nature and natural resources. 
To address this, TML has been 
working on the corporate engagement 
programme of Science-Based Targets 
for Nature. This structured approach 
will help us better understand, manage 
and reduce our contribution to the key 
drivers of nature loss. During FY26, 
we completed an assessment of the 
material impacts of our operations and 
our immediate upstream value chain on 
nature and biodiversity, establishing an 
important foundation for future action 
and target setting.

2nd Integrated Annual Report 2025-26
=== page 70 ===
Beyond Value Chain
We are demonstrating leadership by 
addressing nature and biodiversity 
beyond our operations and value chain, 
aligned with our ambition to create 
meaningful impact at scale. Following 
a detailed evaluation of potential focus 
areas, we identified three flagship 
projects that support the goals of the 
Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity 
Framework.
Wetlands and Winged Voyagers 
Wetlands located along India’s section 
of the Central Asian Flyway serve as 
critical wintering habitats for millions 
of migratory birds, providing food, 
shelter and resting grounds essential for 
their annual journeys. Protecting these 
ecosystems is vital for sustaining global 
migration pathways and preserving 
avian biodiversity.
In partnership with Wetlands 
International South Asia, we launched 
the Wetlands and Winged Voyagers 
initiative with the ambition of creating 
wetland-positive landscapes within 
a 100-km radius of our production 
facilities in Pune, Lucknow and 
Jamshedpur. These landscapes were 
studied using satellite image analysis, 
thematic overlays and on-ground 
ecological evaluation. This led to 
mapping of around 11,800 Wetlands 
across 15 sub-basins spanning over 
four major rivers. Building on this 
assessment, 1,843 wetlands were 
evaluated on the ground and classified 
into 9 hydrogeomorphic categories to 
support function-based management. 
We further assessed 300 priority 
wetlands spanning nearly 70,000 
hectares to establish their ecological 
character and develop wetland health 
cards. In addition, 75 framework 
management plans are being prepared 
for high-priority wetlands in Jharkhand, 
Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat 
in collaboration with the respective 
State Wetland Authorities, providing 
a roadmap for long-term conservation 
and sustainable use.
The Asian Waterbird Census (AWC) 2025 
was carried on these landscapes by 
sensitising and capacity building of TML 
employees. A total of 451 employees 
and 64 expert birders participated in the 
workshops and were trained to execute 
standardised waterbird monitoring in 
accordance with AWC protocols; the 
survey recorded 225 waterbird species 
counting approximately 1,17,000 individual waterbirds, including 100+ 
migratory species from CAF and 16 
globally threatened bird species.
Maximus 
Asian elephants, recognised as India’s 
national heritage animal, play a vital 
ecological role as a keystone species 
that supports ecosystem health and 
biodiversity conservation. Through 
Project Maximus, we are contributing 
to elephant conservation across two 
important landscapes: the Singhbhum 
Elephant Reserve in Jharkhand and the 
Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve in southern 
India. 
In Jharkhand, we are working with 
Aaranyak as our technical partner to 
develop a practical and science-based 
elephant conservation plan for the 
Ranchi and Singhbhum regions. The 
project includes ecological assessments, 
habitat evaluations, threat analyses 
and studies of human-elephant conflict 
from both ecological and community 
perspectives. The objective is to 
support viable elephant populations 
while promoting coexistence in shared 
landscapes. Currently, detailed field 
surveys, which include ecological, 
human perception and focused group 
discussions as well as GIS mapping 
are in progress in over 20,000 sq km 
area covering 13 Forest Divisions of 
Jharkhand.
The project is expected to generate 
updated scientific baselines, map 
elephant habitats, migration 
corridors and conflict zones and develop site-specific and regional 
mitigation measures that can serve as 
scalable models for human-elephant 
coexistence.
Go Green 
Natural habitats across Northeast 
India face increasing pressure from 
deforestation, shortened shifting 
cultivation cycles and expanding 
infrastructure development. Through 
our flagship Go Green initiative, 
implemented in partnership with 
Lemsachenlok, a grassroots community 
organisation, we are supporting large-
scale ecological restoration in the 
Longleng district of Nagaland.
During FY25, we planted and 
maintained 5.5 lakh saplings, followed 
by an additional 6.0 lakh saplings in 
FY26. Collectively, the programme 
has enabled the plantation of 11.5 
lakh saplings and the protection 
of approximately 1,150 acres of 
community land.
The initiative focuses on restoring 
degraded jhum fallow lands through 
community-led plantation efforts that 
combine scientific restoration practices 
with indigenous knowledge systems. 
By prioritising native tree species, the 
project is helping restore ecological 
integrity, enhance biodiversity and 
improve landscape resilience. At the 
same time, it supports the livelihoods 
and cultural traditions of indigenous 
communities that depend on forest 
ecosystems for their well-being and 
sustenance.

Our Future of Work initiatives focus on building an agile, digital and future-

inclusion and experience to create a more engaging and resilient workplace.Kaushalya Programme 
The ‘Kaushalya’ programme (Earn 
While Learn) is a first-of-its-kind 
initiative designed to build industry-
ready talent from rural India. What 
began as a skilling intervention has 
evolved into a scaled inclusion and 
capability-building platform. Over 9,000

27% gender representation and 26%

(AA), expanding access to opportunities 
for underrepresented groups.

2–3-year Diploma in Mechatronics 
Engineering from reputed universities. 
This integrated model ensures 
practical, application-led learning 
alongside formal education. With a 
100% placement rate, the programme 
equips participants with technical 
skills, workplace readiness and the 
ability to operate effectively in an 
industrial environment. It also creates 
opportunities for long-term career 
growth and upward mobility, extending 
its impact beyond individuals to their 
families. Through Kaushalya, we

Full-Time Apprentice  
(FTA) Scheme
Our Full-Time Apprentice (FTA) Scheme 
is a structured programme under the 
Apprenticeship Act, 1961, designed to 
build a strong talent pipeline for our 
Manufacturing, Quality and Service 
functions. The two-year programme 
focuses on developing skilled craftsmen 
in emerging and high-demand areas 
such as Auto Electrical and Electronics, 
Mechatronics and High Voltage 
Systems (EV).
Future-focused trades, including 
Vehicle Software Technicians and 
Additive Manufacturing Technicians, 
are being developed in collaboration 
with government agencies, ensuring 
alignment with evolving industry 
requirements. The programme 
combines technical training at 
plant-based training centres, hands-
on experience in manufacturing 
environments and exposure to service 
operations. A structured governance 
framework monitors academic 
performance, practical skills, discipline 
and development of soft skills. In 
addition to technical capabilities, 
apprentices receive training in safety, 
communication, problem-solving, TQM, 
Kaizen, WCQ and other operational 
excellence methodologies.
We currently have 216 FTAs in the 
programme, with women accounting 
for 50% of participants. Four of our 
six manufacturing locations have all-
women FTA batches. Upon successful 
completion, top-performing apprentices 
are offered roles in key operational

Succession Planning
Organisation Talent Review (OTR) and Succession Planning are annual processes at Tata Motors to review, identify and develop 
talent for leadership roles, with the objective of ensuring management continuity and enabling the right people to take up the 
right positions at the right time. Inputs from OTR and succession planning processes drive actionable development plans to 
ensure qualitative completion of development goals for successors through

FY26 Safety, Health and 
Wellbeing Update
We operate with an unwavering 
belief that safety and well-being are 
non-negotiable conditions of doing 
business and are integral to our 
strategic roadmap. This commitment 
is embedded across all business 
verticals—from manufacturing 
and mobility services to product 
development and after-sales—ensuring 
that safety is intrinsically integrated 
into every decision, operation and 
stakeholder engagement.
Our approach is anchored in a robust 
Occupational Health and Safety 
Management System aligned with 
ISO 45001:2018, complemented by a 
comprehensive Safety Management 
System built on Tata Group Safety 
Standards and DuPont Sustainable 
Solutions (dss+). Guided by a strong 
Safety and Health Policy and an 
established Safety Culture Model, the 
framework fosters active employee 
participation at all levels and drives 
our pursuit of a Zero Harm culture. All 
manufacturing facilities are certified to 
ISO 45001:2018, reinforcing a strong 
foundation for continuous improvement 
in safety performance.
A multi-tiered Safety and Health 
governance framework ensures 
leadership accountability and effective 
execution across the organisation. Apex-level oversight is provided by the 
SHS Committee of the Board, chaired 
by an Independent Director and is 
reinforced through SHS Councils led 
by senior leadership, Corporate Sub-
Committees led by Plant Heads and 
Apex Committees at manufacturing 
locations. In addition, five Corporate 
Sub-Committees led by senior leaders 
drive focused interventions aligned 
to strategic priorities, adopting a 
structured Plan–Do–Check–Act 
(PDCA) approach to enable continuous 
improvement and horizontal 
deployment.
To strengthen implementation and 
employee engagement, 17 operational 
safety standards have been deployed 
across the organisation, supported 
by a robust governance ecosystem 
comprising Broad-Based Teams (BBTs), 
Factory Implementation Committees 
(FICs), Self-Directed Teams (SDTs) and 
Self-Managed Teams (SMTs). In line with 
evolving business requirements, we 
have also introduced additional safety 
standards addressing alternative  
fuel operations.
We advance our safety maturity through 
strategic alignment, behavioural 
transformation and digital integration. 
A comprehensive Safety System 
Assessment conducted in partnership 
with dss+ across key pillars—Leadership, 
Integrated Governance, Incident 
Management and Business Partner 
Management—has reinforced strong strategic intent, governance alignment 
and visible leadership commitment at 
all levels.
Digital enablement remains a key lever 
in strengthening safety performance. 
Our internally developed Safety 
Portal supports end-to-end safety 
management processes, including 
standards and procedures management, 
incident investigation, safety 
observations, business partner safety 
management, training and capability 
building and health management. 
Enabled with advanced analytics and 
AI-driven tools, the platform facilitates 
real-time reporting, enhanced risk 
identification and data-driven decision-
making across managerial levels.
Beyond manufacturing, our Safety 
and Health function extends coverage 
to non-manufacturing Operations, 
working closely with workshops, 
warehouses, fleet Operations, depot 
management, offices and regional 
service organisations. Workshops, being 
the largest segment, are progressively 
adopting critical safety parameters 
and mandatory standards through 
the central safety portal, ensuring a 
consistent and integrated approach to 
safety across the value chain.
Through these integrated efforts, we 
have improved our safety culture, 
enhanced governance effectiveness and 
progressed our journey towards a Zero 
Harm workplace.

Leadership and Governance
At Tata Motors, we embed safety and health as core business priorities through strong leadership commitment, structured 
governance and deep workforce participation across all levels of the organisation.
Our safety culture is driven through a multi-tier governance framework led by senior leadership and supported by corporate sub-
committees, plant-level forums and cross-functional teams that ensure continuous review of safety performance and systematic 
deployment of preventive actions and learnings.
At the plant level, this structure is 
further strengthened through the 
formation of Self-Managed Teams 
(SMTs) and Self-Directed Teams (SDTs) 
comprising business partner employees 
and blue-collar workforce. These teams 
are established to actively involve 
employees in safety management, 
strengthen ownership at the shopfloor and ensure effective implementation 
and cascading of safety initiatives across 
operational areas.
Leadership-led initiatives such as SAFE 
(Safety Awareness and Felt Leadership 
Excellence), 90 Minutes of Care, 
structured capability building and 
horizontal deployment of learnings 
continue to reinforce a strong culture of engagement, accountability and 
proactive risk management.
We further institutionalise safety 
performance through its integration 
into Corporate and Plant Balanced 
Scorecards, ensuring sustained focus 
on safety outcomes, continuous 
improvement and alignment with our 
Zero Harm aspiration.**

The risk assessment is done through 
Hazard Identification and Risk 
Assessment (HIRA) standard that 
incorporates all activities involved in 
identifying hazards and evaluating risk 
at facilities throughout their life cycle. 
This ensures that risks to employees, 
to public and the environment are 
consistently controlled within the 
organisation’s risk tolerance. The 
HIRA standard guides the assessment 
methodology for each of the activities 
in manufacturing operations.Objective of HIRA study is to: 
All plants are certified to ISO 45001. Hazards are identified and significant risks are acted upon as part of a continuous process.
For non-routine activities, work permits, Job Safety Analysis (JSA) and Take 2 standards are adopted to manage risk. Safety 
observations, Business Partner Field Safety Assessment (BPFSA) and audits are carried out on a regular basis. Incident learning 
and sharing are conducted across all plants, shops and office locations.Tata Motors implemented a systematic and dynamic HIRA process to proactively identify, assess 
and control workplace hazards.
Carry out a systematic, critical appraisal of all potential hazards involving 
personnel, plant, services and operating methods 
Identify the existing safeguards available to control the risks due to the 
hazards 
Suggest additional control measures to eliminate the risk or to reduce the risk 
to acceptable level 
Prepare a HIRA that helps in continuously monitoring these risks, detect any 
changes and ensure the controls are effective.
A cross-functional team is formed to brainstorm and identify 
all hazards. All activities are mapped and hazards are 
identified for each of these activities based on the nature of 
the activity, history of incidents and experience of workers. 
For all such identified hazards, risk is calculated based on 
severity and likelihood. The unit of measure of risk is the Risk 
Priority Number (RPN).Risk Priority Number (RPN) = Likelihood X Severity. 
{Where Severity= Scale of Risk X Level of Harm X No of  
People Affected}
Every risk is categorised into Trivial, Tolerable, Moderate, 
Substantial and Intolerable. These hazards are then mitigated HIRA process flow

Business Partner Safety 
Management
Contractors are referred to as Business 
Partners at Tata Motors and the safety 
of the Business Partner workforce is a 
key priority in driving safety across the 
organisation. Business Partner safety is 
managed through a Business Partners 
Safety Management (BPSM) Standard. 
The intent of the standard is to ensure 
There is a robust six step process to manage Business Partners’ safety:
Business Partner selection 
procedure (PQ) is focused on 
the critical evaluation of safety 
performance criteria (Lead 
and Lag indicators) and the 
integration of new systems into 
the sourcing process.
Orientation and Training: Business 
Partners’ pre-selection, contract 
preparation a nd contract award 
culminate effectively at this point 
and contract workers embrace 
the ‘safety culture’ of the site 
and location-specific safety 
requirements durin g the initial 
orientation and training.
Periodic evaluation:  Developed with the intent that 
the Business Partner improves future performance 
and the asset owner improves the contracting 
process. Further, the intent of this procedure is also 
to obtain feedback on Business Partners’ safety 
performance, establishing whether that performance 
is adequate to remain as an “approved business 
partner” and setting up the means for updating the 
relevant information in the TML Business Partner 
registration database.
The safety performance of Business Partners is 
tracked using tools such as monthly evaluations, 
quarterly star ratings for Categories A and D and 
quarterly SMT maturity assessments. Daily work 
management focuses on monitoring leading 
indicators such as near misses, unsafe conditions, 
incident reporting and lessons learned. Inputs from 
incident investigations, safety standards, training 
and observations are used to provide feedback and 
support ongoing improvement.Contract preparation is designed 
to establish guidelines for creating 
contract packages that define safety 
expectations aligned with specific 
contracting requirements and to 
provide clarity on the application 
and enforcement of safety 
obligations within the contract.
Managing the Work: Developed with the intent to uniformly and 
consistently manage work across all TML sites, which includes 
assessing in the field the Business Partner’s safety execution against 
contract requirements, assuring that field audits (BPFSA) and safety 
visits are directed at injury prevention rather than “policing” and, 
most importantly, installing a follow-up process that drives continuous 
improvement and avoids repetition of common errors. Contract award (Pre-Bid meeting) 
is done based on evaluation from 
steps 1 and 2 including Safety 
expectations become a part of 
contract document.1

We promote a partnership-based approach by fostering 
dignity and inclusion. The shift from “Contractors” to 
“Business Partners” reflects a culture of respect, equity and 
shared accountability. Business Partners—including suppliers, 
logistics providers and scrap dealers—are treated as integral 
members of our extended workforce.Their engagement spans safety reviews, audits, star ratings 
and field assessments, enabling active participation in safety 
outcomes. Structured training, transparent evaluation 
processes, clearly defined responsibilities and fair consequence 
management frameworks reinforce ownership. Data 
transparency through KPIs and dashboards further enables 
performance visibility and improvement. This approach drives 
a transition from compliance-based oversight to collaborative 
safety excellence.
